chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn Yahya, both together, from Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'd, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Salamah, from Muhammad ibn Sa'id ibn Ghazwan, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abu Khadijah, who said:

I entered upon Abi al-Hasan عليه السلام, and he said to me: "Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has strengthened the believer with a spirit from Him. It is present with him at every time in which he does good and is Godwary, and it is absent from him at every time in which he sins and transgresses. So it is with him, trembling with joy at his doing good, and sinking into the earth at his doing evil."

So take care, O servants of Allah, of His blessings by rectifying yourselves; you will increase in certainty and gain a precious and valuable profit. May Allah have mercy on a man who intended good and then did it, or intended evil and then refrained from it.
Then he said: "We strengthen the spirit through obedience to Allah and working for Him."

key_terms.اَلْمُؤْمِنَ: the believer who is divinely strengthened
key_terms.بِرُوحٍ: with a spirit by which the believer is supported
key_terms.يَتَّقِي: he is Godwary and guards himself from sin
key_terms.يَقِينًا: certainty and firm conviction in faith

ai.seo_question: How does Allah support the believer according to this hadith from al-Kafi?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that the believer is supported by a divine spirit that accompanies him in moments of obedience and taqwa, but withdraws at times of sin and transgression. It exhorts believers to preserve Allah’s blessings through self-rectification, increase in certainty, and restrain themselves from evil while acting upon good.

en.hubeali: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, and Muhammad Bin Yahya, altogether from Ali Bin Muhammad Bin Sa’ad, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, from Abu Salma, from Muhammad Bin Saeed Bin Gazwan, from Ibn Abu Najran, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Abu Khadeeja who said,

‘I went over to Abu Al-Hassanasws, and heasws said to me: ‘Allahazwj Blessed and High Aids the Momin with a spirit from Himazwj, cautioning him during every time he does a good deed in it, and it is absent from him during every time he sins in it and transgresses. So it is with him, vibrating joyfully during his good deeds and falling into the earth during his sinning.

Therefore, make a pact for His<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Blessings, servants of Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup>, by correcting yourselves, you will be increasing your conviction and you will be profiting by a good price. May Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> have Mercy upon a man who thinks of doing good, so he does it, or thinks of doing evil, but retracts from it’.

Then said: We<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> assist the spirit by the obedience to Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> and working for Him<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 1. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn Yahya have all narrated from Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Sa’d from Muhammad ibn Muslim from abu Salmah from Muhammad ibn Sa’id ibn Ghazwan from ibn abu Najran from Muhammad ibn Sinan from abu Khadijah who has said the following:

“Once I went to see abu al-Hassan (a.s.) and he said to me, ‘Allah, the Most Blessed, the Most High, supports a believer with a spirit from His side who attends him in all times that he performs a good deed and observes piety. The spirit remains absent in all times that he commits sins and transgresses. The spirit vibrates with joy when he does a good deed and turns into a despicable thing and lowly to earth when he commits a sin.

O servants of Allah, be committed to benefit from the favors of Allah to correct and reform yourselves; it (commitment) will increase your certainty and you earn fine and valuable things. May Allah grant favors to those who think of doing good and perform it or think of committing something bad, but refrain and desist.’
The Imam then said, ‘We support and strengthen the spirit by means of obeying Allah and working for Him.’”
